definitions.gloss: mixed ground meat; ground meat blend of beef and pork
definitions.explanation: Ground meat that combines beef and pork, typically in roughly equal proportions. A staple in Japanese home cooking, used for hamburger steaks, meatballs, and other dishes.

examples.japanese: {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}を{買|か}う。
ハンバーグには{合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}がよく{合|あ}う。
examples.english: Mixed ground meat works well for hamburger steaks.

examples.japanese: {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}に{塩|しお}コショウと{卵|たまご}を{加|くわ}えてよくこねる。
examples.english: Add salt, pepper, and egg to the mixed ground meat and knead well.

notes:
A compound of {合|あい} (combined/together) + {挽|び}き (ground/minced). Almost always used with {肉|にく} as {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}. The standard ratio is roughly 50-50 or 60-40 beef to pork.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}: mixed ground meat
- {合挽|あいび}きミンチ: mixed minced meat
- {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく}のハンバーグ: hamburger steak made with mixed ground meat

USAGE:
In Japanese supermarkets, ground meat is typically sold as {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく} (beef), {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく} (pork), {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく} (chicken), or {合挽|あいび}き{肉|にく} (mixed beef and pork). The blend gives dishes more richness than either meat alone.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ひき{肉|にく}: ground meat — the general term for any ground/minced meat
- ミンチ: mince — loanword for ground meat, used interchangeably with ひき{肉|にく}
